content:
MS NOW host Nicolle Wallace expressed concern Tuesday over President Donald Trump and his trip to Asia, arguing the MAGA leader could act erratically after his party’s midterms defeat — and prioritize his amicable relationships with foreign authoritarian leaders over national security.

“Trump appears incapable or perhaps unwilling to adequately manage the growing scandal engulfing his own administration related to allegations that a Chinese asset or spy infiltrated the upper echelons of one of America’s most vital tech companies, Nvidia,” said Wallace.

The “Deadline: White House” host continued Tuesday, “So while Trump goes about deal-making and legacy-building, the American people who very recently rejected his vision for our future are left to wonder what sorts of deals he’s about to make on our behalf.”

Trump is currently in Asia for high-profile diplomatic summits including foreign leaders such as Russia’s Vladimir Putin, China’s Xi Jinping and potentially North Korean dictator Kim Jong Un — after a major scandal concerning Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang.

Huang resigned last week as CEO amid allegations that one of the subjects of his extramarital affairs was a spy from China, and that this facilitated the purchase of at least $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia chips in the ongoing AI race between China and the U.S.

Trump reportedly urged Huang not to resign once his affair with the alleged spy became public and told reporters Monday, “I haven’t heard that, no. I don’t know that she is a spy.” Wallace suggested this was part of Trump’s penchant for appeasing foreign leaders he likes.

It read, “Trump’s swing through Asia this week puts on full display his foreign policy driven by securing deals over diplomatic strategy, with the president repeatedly setting aside national security concerns to stay close to powerful leaders and the corporate titans who court him.”

The Wall Street Journal noted further, “Trump’s first trip abroad since the midterms ... is being scrutinized by allies and rivals alike. With no more elections to face, Trump could become more willing to take risks or escalate conflicts abroad, U.S. and foreign officials say.”

MS NOW senior White House reporter Vaughn Hillyard cited senior administration officials to Wallace who said Trump is unlikely to discuss Russia’s war on Ukraine or China’s alleged spy during the trip — because he wants to maintain his “personal” relationships with them.

Trump has told reporters he might discuss both issues, however, prompting Hillyard to suggest he’s publicly feigning to potentially hold Xi and Putin to task while privately appeasing them.

“I … feel like I’ve lost the plot,” Wallace reacted. “The Republicans in Congress are complicit with the United States of America going completely flaccid in its national security, economic security and AI posture against China. For Pete’s sake, do they care about nothing?”

She continued, “Politically? Economically? Or security-wise?”

Hillyard noted Tuesday that Trump has a penchant for appeasement with strongmen leaders and dictators, even if that means allies “economically and militarily” distancing themselves from the U.S., and that Trump has touted his “good relationship” with Xi, Putin and Kim.

He argued Trump prioritizing his standing with these leaders doesn’t just have implications for U.S. national security, but for that of America’s allies —as Russia “continues to kill tens of thousands of Ukrainians” and “China continues to threaten Taiwan.”

“The issue for Donald Trump here, Nicolle, is that in his version and view of this, having a ‘good relationship’ is having engagement,” Hillyard said Tuesday. “And it is an ignorance of the realities that are actually inhibiting the pathway to peace.”
